The polling suggests Trump enters Labor Day in a substantially weaker position than when he returned to office and in a weaker position than before his first midterm election.

At a comparable point before the 2018 midterms, Civiqs recorded Trump at 43 percent approval and 53 percent disapproval, a net rating of minus 10.

Today, Trump stands at minus 26 nationally. [...] The data comes from Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. A Newsweek analysis compares Trump's approval rating on September 4, 2026, with where it stood when he returned to office on January 20, 2025, using net approval calculated as approve minus disapprove.

In Indiana, Trump's net approval rating slipped underwater in Civiqs' polling in late June, after being positive throughout his second term. It now stands at -3.

Similarly, in Mississippi, his net approval, which had been positive during much of his second administration, has been in negative territory since May.
